source_snapshot.procedure: Attach the BMC UART, set the TFTP server, obtain DHCP, TFTP the BMC binary to RAM address 0x83000000, probe SPI flash 0, write 0x4000000 bytes from RAM to flash offset 0, save the U-Boot environment, reset, and check BMC function after reboot.
source_snapshot.criteria: Firmware is flashed successfully, with generic result/photo and unexpected-log collection.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; assigns the physical UART/U-Boot flash to an operator and proposes `ipmitool mc info` after reboot, while correctly warning that the destructive action can brick the BMC.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED with CRITICAL risk; requires an approved image, checksum, board compatibility, exact write length, stable power, recovery and explicit approval before the literal UART sequence.
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Procedure: ----------- 1. Plug BMC uart console. 2. Send command to flash BMC: setenv serverip <TFTP Server>​ dhcp​ tftp 0x83000000 [BMC BINARY]​ sf probe 0​ sf update 0x83000000 0 0x4000000​ saveenv​ reset 3. After BMC reboot , check BMC function should work normally.

source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Uboot flash: plug the BMC UART console and flash the BMC image through the uBoot TFTP/sf flow. The flash steps are done over the physical BMC UART console by an operator; the agent only stages the image and verifies the BMC responds afterwards OOB from the agent host: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -Ei 'Firmware Revision' 2>&1

disposition_reason: `tftp` reports an actual transfer byte count, whereas `sf update ... 0x4000000` always consumes 64 MiB from RAM. If the binary is shorter, trailing RAM contents can be written; if the board's SPI map differs, an offset-zero full-span write can overwrite U-Boot, environment, recovery or board data. `sf probe 0` also proves only that some device was selected unless JEDEC identity/capacity are matched. Finally, `saveenv` after setting `serverip` and using DHCP can persist temporary lab networking. Therefore the review must bind every destructive parameter to a signed board package, control environment persistence and retain independent recovery, while a responding BMC remains evidence rather than an automatic PASS. test_case.purpose: Demonstrate that a board-compatible BMC image can be transferred through BMC U-Boot/TFTP, written to the intended SPI flash region, rebooted, and returned to normal out-of-band management operation on the intended firmware.
required_package: SUT, board revision, BMC/SoC and SPI bus/chip-select/JEDEC identity with complete flash-region map
Approved BMC binary filename, target version, exact byte length, hash/signature and board/bootloader compatibility
Approved RAM load address, flash offset/length and policy for preserving bootloader, environment, recovery, calibration and configuration regions
TFTP network plan, UART settings, stable power/maintenance window and qualified operator
Full backup, golden image, dual-bank or external programmer recovery procedure and maximum reboot/recovery timeout
Secure BMC credential injection and expected post-flash firmware, active bank, network/configuration, service, sensor and log oracle
test_case.test_command: Identify the exact SUT/BMC/SPI target and active/recovery layout; back up required flash/environment/configuration data; verify the approved image, signature/hash, byte length and RAM load address; attach UART and stable recovery power; let a qualified operator execute the source TFTP, probe and approved bounded write once; avoid persisting temporary network variables unless explicitly required; reset and verify firmware identity, boot mode, management services, network/configuration, sensors, inventory and logs against the baseline.
